description: Peer -> Master observability evidence: how a peer pushes status/metrics/liveness/checkpoint/inbox-alert reports to the Master, which records them and acts on nothing. The reference implementation is shared/sparknet-authz.py (build_telemetry_report / verify_telemetry_report); this file is the normative statement. Design and rationale: MASTER_OBSERVABILITY_DESIGN.md (fabric Step 69).

implementation_state.checkpoint_anchor: implemented (fabric Step 70E) — peer-node/services/sparknet-checkpoint-anchor.py appends an idempotent signed checkpoint over the ledger head (shared/sparknet-provenance.py build_checkpoint_data/append_block) and pushes the full signed block as payload {checkpoint: block}. A re-run over an unchanged head writes no block and re-pushes the same evidence; an empty chain is silent. Live cross-node anchoring is DoD: confirm: user.
implementation_state.consumers: status and metrics are produced by 70A; liveness by 70D; checkpoint anchors by 70E; the inbox arrival alert by 70F; the status payload's trust summary by 70G (no new kind); metrics carries the local idle evidence from 9B (no new kind).
implementation_state.idle_evidence: implemented (Master Step 9B) — the metrics payload carries `idle` {schema_version, sampled_at, interactive_sessions, ssh_sessions, gpu_probe, gpu_util_pct, wg_interface, wg_rx_bytes, wg_tx_bytes, wg_peer_count, errors[]}. shared/sparknet-idle.py measures the host; a probe that cannot answer is null plus an error, never zero. It never returns an idle/busy verdict: the nocturnal scheduler owns thresholds and the all-nodes conjunction. WireGuard counters are null when the unprivileged pusher cannot read `wg show`; the scheduler must obtain authoritative counters without granting the peer service new privilege.
implementation_state.envelope: implemented (fabric Step 69B) — shared/sparknet-authz.py builds and verifies a report
implementation_state.honest_pair: implemented reference envelope, pusher, liveness, checkpoint-anchor, inbox-alert and flagged-surfacing paths, nothing deployed here; the cross-node legs are a human's to confirm on a live pair
implementation_state.inbox_alert: implemented (fabric Step 70F) — the peer guard's installed RFI answer calls sparknet-telemetry-push.py to emit kind=inbox_alert with payload {item, source, request_id, content_sha256, audit_block}. It is gated on telemetry, unsigned and overlay-attributed, and never affects acceptance: a failed push leaves the item installed and the local 67B spool/ping unchanged. Live cross-node delivery is DoD: confirm: user.
implementation_state.liveness: implemented (fabric Step 70D) — peer-node/services/sparknet-liveness-monitor.py runs the shared ContinuousMonitor against signature-checked registry peers, answers probes on the contracted non-serving port 4211, and pushes kind=liveness with payload {observer, probe_port, claims[]}. The claim is unsigned and overlay-attributed; the probe port is contracted in ports.json. Live cross-node behaviour is DoD: confirm: user.
implementation_state.listener: implemented (fabric Steps 69C, 70B) — master-node/services/sparknet-peer-intake.py binds the overlay only and serves POST /api/v1/telemetry and POST /api/v1/rfi-request; contracts/ports.json marks 8090 implemented. The unit is staged by `make -C master-node peer-intake-unit`, not enabled.
implementation_state.pusher: implemented (fabric Steps 70A, 9B) — peer-node/services/sparknet-telemetry-push.py builds status and metrics with the shared envelope and posts them, gated on the telemetry capability. Metrics now carries shared/sparknet-idle.py evidence (session/GPU/WireGuard probes); a failed idle probe is null plus an error and cannot silence the report. A peer without telemetry exits silently.
implementation_state.status: implemented (fabric Steps 70A, 70G) — payload {node_id, role, overlay_ipv4, capabilities[], trust{level, retained_flags[], flagged_shares[]}}. The trust summary is read from the share records the bridge persisted and summarized by peer-node/services/sparknet-share-regime.py::trust_summary. It is a belief, never a permission: the console only surfaces it, and only a Master-signed registry event moves a level.

refusals.malformed: not an object, wrong field set, a required field empty or non-string, kind outside the vocabulary, or payload not an object
refusals.not_yet_valid: issued_at is further in the future than the skew allowance
refusals.off_overlay: the source is not a registered, non-revoked peer overlay address — refused by the listener's source gate before the body is read
refusals.replayed_nonce: this nonce has already been seen on this node
refusals.wrong_peer: peer_fingerprint is not the overlay-derived fingerprint of the sender

report.attribution: the authenticated overlay, NOT a signature — see MASTER_OBSERVABILITY_DESIGN.md and RFI_REQUEST_DESIGN.md (Step 68A). The Master derives the sender's fingerprint from the WireGuard-authenticated source address via its own registry (overlay_ipv4 -> fingerprint) and refuses a report whose peer_fingerprint field disagrees. Nothing binds a peer fingerprint to a node signing public key, so a node-key signature would be unverifiable theatre; on the overlay the tunnel is the identity.
report.direction: peer -> Master, onto the Master's peer-intake listener (8090 re-scoped, POST /api/v1/telemetry)
report.kinds_note: A closed vocabulary. kind routes the report to what records it; the per-kind payload's meaning belongs to the consumer sub-step (70A status/metrics, 70D liveness, 70E checkpoint_anchor, 70F inbox_alert), not to the envelope, so a new kind's internals never reshape it.
report.no_authority: a telemetry report cannot grant, revoke, escalate, widen a permission or approve a guard application. The Master records it as evidence and may surface or flag; it never acts on it as authority. Any leg that would let observability touch an authority path is a contract change with its own step.
report.payload: an opaque JSON object. The envelope validates only that it IS an object; each kind's payload shape is the consumer's contract.
report.unsigned: the report carries no signature_b64, and there is deliberately no sign_telemetry_report. nonce + expires_at are the replay/freshness guard a signed envelope's freshness fields would otherwise be.
report.verify: shared/sparknet-authz.py::verify_telemetry_report — a validator + fingerprint match, not a signature check: exact field set, kind in the vocabulary, payload an object, peer_fingerprint == the overlay-derived expected_fingerprint, expiry, future-issue skew, nonce replay. Returns (ok, reason); never raises.

transport.capability: telemetry (peer-held): a peer without it does not push. Distinct from admin-supervise (Master-held), which gates the PULL feed (list_events over the bridge /admin/*) — push and pull are complementary, and the capability split is the point.
transport.implementation_state: the envelope, the re-scoped 8090 listener, the peer pusher, liveness, checkpoint anchors, the inbox alert and flagged surfacing are implemented; all live cross-node legs remain a human's to confirm
transport.note: The Master's peer-intake listener, re-scoped from the superseded instant-push (8090) — which resolves Master Step 7's open 'survives / re-scoped / retired' question. Overlay-only, source-gated to registered non-revoked peers. Fabric Step 70B joins the RFI request route (/api/v1/rfi-request) to the same listener and renames the service to sparknet-peer-intake, so the two families build one surface rather than two.

why: Phase 4 is Master observability WITHOUT touching the data path. Peers talk directly by design and the Master is authority-plane only at 10.100.0.1/32, so monitoring is signed evidence pushed to the Master, never interception. Telemetry carries no authority: it informs, records, surfaces and flags; it never grants, revokes, escalates, widens a permission or approves a guard application.
